title: Graph run record
description: One run directory: graph.yaml, checks.yaml, progress.yaml, framing.yaml, rules.yaml, lessons.yaml. Each file is a top-level key. Cross-file constraints that JSON Schema cannot express are listed under x-crossfile and enforced by validate.py.

subagent_id.description: Opaque identifier returned by the runtime; preserve verbatim (Claude hex, Codex UUID or task path).

content.description: exec: the command. inspect: the property. review: the property under review.

exec_available.description: Decided per check at design time. yes: a program returns the fails_when verdict (type exec). no: no program can return it; type is inspect or review and node.unavailable.tried records each program considered and what it returned. partial: a program flags candidates but cannot return the verdict for them (type exec); every flagged item is adjudicated by a review gate recorded as a <id>-residue row (X28)

residue.description: exec_available partial only. The residue review's real artifact is the program's flagged list; its mutant is that list with one real violation added (a sentence that breaks fails_when, placed with a false location); the reviewer receives both unlabeled in random order per layer_5_gates and must fail the mutant and pass the list. This field states, in one line, how the adjudication is briefed (the check text the reviewer judges against)

gate.description: the id of the node's exec check that gates it; a node with several exec checks names one

unavailable.description: Programs considered and what each returned, for every check on this node with exec_available no; filled at design time; an analysis of what a program would return is enough when running it would cost a node run

model.description: tier index = len(tier_rule) + escalations, capped at the last index of the MODELS ladder (index 0 = cheapest); validate.py checks the arithmetic (X08)

tier_rule.description: the lines that fired at dispatch; frozen — a check_revision after dispatch does not rewrite them (X25 exempts a node with a check_revision decision)

escalations.description: count of tier-up retries (hypothesis cause under_capacity; in prompt v3.0 this is the tier-up form of cause (a); in v2.x it was cause (d))

item.description: the {{CHECKS}} item id, for kind acceptance

kind.description: na_code is reserved for the well-formedness audit entry in progress; rows never use it

from_check.description: the carried node check (required by X11 when from_node has more than one check and no code.gate)

exercises.description: rules.yaml ids; empty means acceptance only. Acceptance rows only.

unchecked_rules.description: rules (by id) that no check exercises, listed before approval with the reason, and reported at delivery (X32)

phase.description: set instead of node for a reviewer or auditor dispatched outside any node

reserve_runs.description: runs spent from the reserve (the last tenth of limit, rounded up) or past it: a one-item correction return or its re-gate (node + attempt >= 2), the integration node's run (attempt >= 1, no node), or an audit (name, no attempt). Audits are the only runs that may take consumed past limit (X30)

kind.description: ruling: an interpretation the lead adds to a brief (of an input fact, a check term, or a source), recorded before dispatch with node or phase; its reason holds the reading and the text it applies to

phase.description: set instead of node for a decision taken outside any node

disposition.description: asked: put to the person and answered (answer required). assumed: not asked; the assumption is stated in answer-less form by the assumptions list or here. pending: put to the person, answer not yet received — legal only while progress.next_action.kind is blocked (X29)

issue.description: pending only: the open_issues id the question is carried by

section.description: section of the spec; empty string means the spec is unsectioned

x-crossfile: X01 every graph node has, for EACH of its checks, a checks row with subject.kind=node, subject.check=that check, attempt=1
X02 every reads.upstream.node exists; every reads.upstream.sections item is in that node's shape, compared as exact strings
X03 every split_reason.risk exists in framing.risks; every split_reason.nodes item exists
X04 every framing.risks[].guarded_by gate names an existing node and one of its checks
X05 every isolation.subagent and audits.evidence.isolation.subagent exists in progress.subagents
X06 for each node, no subagent is both builder and reviewer
X07 reviewer_tier index >= model.tier index on the MODELS ladder
X08 model.tier index == min(len(tier_rule) + escalations, last index) on the MODELS ladder, index 0 = cheapest; requires --models, otherwise a finding
X09 every checks row exercises[] id exists in rules
X10 progress.graph lists partition the node id set exactly once

X11 (sha compared on the newest carried row per subject; an earlier attempt's carry is history) a carried evidence row's sha256 equals the --artifacts entry for from_node; the carried check is evidence.from_check, else from_node's code.gate, else its only check (several checks with no from_check is a finding); that check's LATEST row has verdict pass; a missing --artifacts entry is a finding

X12 the whole word 'proven' (case-insensitive) appears in no authored record content or comments; only literal source scalar content in rules.rules[*].quote is exempt, without endorsing that quotation
X13 every row with attempt>1 has a hypotheses entry with before_attempt == attempt whose node is the row's subject.node, or subject.item, or the literal 'integration'
X14 writes paths are unique across nodes, compared as exact strings
X15 the reads graph is acyclic
X16 taking each (node, check) subject's LATEST attempt: nodes with a dissent verdict == progress.graph.dissent; nodes with an escalated verdict ⊆ progress.graph.escalated

X17 audits.evidence verdict is pass iff (miscited+unfound)/rows <= 0.10, or rows == 0; audits.wellformed is schema-required on every record; miscited + unfound <= rows; a pass with rows > 0 has fresh_subagent isolation
X18 a node whose checks are all review has a reviewer subagent for that node in progress.subagents once any of its rows has isolation other than not_run (before that, the review has not run)
X19 every rules row with concerns ∋ graph|checks|progress holds on this record — delegated: rules are prose; validator reports them as 'manual'
X20 code node: code.gate names one of the node's checks and that check has type exec
X21 a pass row with exec evidence has actual_exit == expected_exit; a pass row with excerpt evidence has every section verdict pass and at least one section

X22 ids are unique: node ids; check ids within a node; rules ids; open_issues ids; framing assumptions/unknowns/risks ids (one namespace); subagent ids per (id, role, node); (subject, attempt) pairs in checks.rows are unique

X23 every reference resolves whenever present: subject.node/check, decisions.node, hypotheses.node, subagents.node, lessons.node, next_action.node, next_action.issue (open_issues), evidence.from_node. A hypothesis entry's node may also be an acceptance item id (an acceptance review retried after corrections, X13)
X24 every does[].produces is in the node's shape

X25 tier_rule fired lines are consistent with the node as dispatched: review_only_check iff all checks are review; reads_three_or_more_upstream iff len(reads.upstream) >= 3; needs_two_or_more_domains iff len(needs) >= 2; content_merge is not derivable and is accepted as stated. A node with a check_revision decision is exempt: its lines are frozen at dispatch
X26 X17 at rows == 0: verdict must be pass (vacuous) or not_run
X27 progress.assumptions and framing.assumptions share one id namespace; every progress.assumptions id exists in framing.assumptions; a risk or unknown id does not resolve an assumption reference

X28 a check with exec_available partial has, whenever its exec row's actual_exit != expected_exit, a review row for the same subject and attempt whose check id is <id>-residue, with red_evidence of kind mutant (the flagged list plus one added violation) and a fresh_subagent reviewer; the exec row takes that row's verdict. A void residue review is recorded like any void review. A residue row whose verdict is pass or fail is a review with fresh_subagent isolation and mutant red evidence; an unresolved residue row may be degraded

X29 a framing unknown with disposition pending names an open_issues id that exists and is unresolved, and progress.next_action is blocked on that issue; once next_action moves on, the unknown must be asked (with answer) or assumed

X30 when unit is node_runs, usage.reserve_runs holds at most ceil(limit/10) non-audit entries; a correction_return or re_gate names a node with a checks row at that attempt (attempt >= 2); an integration entry names an attempt at which an integration- or acceptance-subject row exists (the integration node's gate is the acceptance items); an audit entry names each audit at most once; consumed exceeds limit by at most the number of audit entries — the reserve is part of limit, audits are the only runs that may pass it
X31 an accepted node's latest row for every check has a verdict other than fail, dissent or escalated (well-formedness, not completion: unresolved rows still make the run partial)

X32 every rules row whose concerns include deliverable is named in some acceptance row's exercises[] or in progress.unchecked_rules (with a reason), and no id is in both; an unchecked_rules id exists in rules
